themes.title: General-purpose humanoids
themes.description: Unitree's Shanghai STAR Market debut (Aug 19, ticker 688836) opened up 629% before paring gains to close +460% at roughly RMB 342B (~$50B) — briefly touching an implied ~$66B intraday — putting the profitable, fast-growing humanoid maker at a reported ~857x 2026 earnings versus the STAR Market's ~130x average. BYD confirmed its first humanoid, "Xiao Di" (1.61m, 58.5kg, real-time translation across six languages), for its Di Space showrooms this month, targeting deployment across 100+ scenarios by year-end. Tesla's Optimus remains unverified: Musk now says output will be "quite slow" given 10,000 unique new parts, with early units routed to an internal "Optimus Academy" training program rather than customers.

themes.title: Warehouse & logistics automation
themes.description: Symbotic's momentum reversed hard this week: shares fell roughly 25% after a surprise SEC filing disclosed a share offering (6.5M Class A shares plus 3.5M more from a SoftBank-controlled holder), and Barclays reaffirmed its Sell rating even after last week's beat-and-raise Q3 FY26 print ($721M revenue, $55M GAAP net income). The stock is now at a fresh 2026 low, down roughly a third for the year — a reminder that a strong quarter doesn't protect against dilution.

themes.title: Surgical robotics
themes.description: Intuitive Surgical fell 5.8% on Aug 20 as a cautious outlook overshadowed an Aug 12 Oppenheimer upgrade to Outperform; shares are down roughly 30% YTD, on pace for the weakest year since 2008, even as procedure growth (+16%) and revenue growth (+18-19%) stay strong and da Vinci 5 just won FDA clearance for cardiac procedures. The competitive backdrop got more concrete too: J&J's Ottava now has FDA de novo authorization for a full slate of soft-tissue procedures — no longer just a threat on paper.

themes.title: Defense autonomy & drones
themes.description: The Trump administration's new drone tariffs took effect Aug 14 — 100% on unmanned systems over 25kg or with "sensitive" features like thermal imaging, 25% on smaller commercial/hobbyist drones — handing AVAV and KTOS a durable US-market pricing edge on top of Kratos's new Army Javelin seeker-upgrade contract and potential $156M DOE Solar Shield award. Pentagon FY27 budget still requests ~$75B for unmanned/counter-drone systems.

themes.title: Field robotics
themes.description: Deere's autonomous articulated dump truck continues quarry operations under its 2nd-gen autonomy kit; Caterpillar's five-machine autonomous construction lineup remains in early rollout. Both stay diversified industrials where robotics is a small slice of the overall return — no fresh sector-specific news this week.

themes.title: Japanese factory automation
themes.description: Keyence hit a fresh limit-up this week on continued double-digit revenue and profit growth, with Fanuc (holding near ¥6,720, 9-buy/1-sell) and Yaskawa (+¥312 to ¥5,462) rallying alongside it as the sector works through the aftermath of Fanuc's Aug 3 guidance shock. Still too early to call it a re-rating rather than a bounce.

themes.title: Supply chain & components
themes.description: Harmonic Drive Systems lifted its full-year guidance Aug 7 on strong automation demand, then struck a more cautious note in its Aug 19 Q1 FY2027 report. HSBC downgraded Cognex to Hold from Buy and cut its price target to $65 from $94 this week, even as the company's new $0.085 dividend went ex-date Aug 20. MP Materials rose 16.4% over the week on a defense offtake deal and Canaccord roadmap commentary, despite still posting a GAAP net loss.

themes.title: The robot "brain"
themes.description: NVIDIA's Jetson Thor platform keeps widening its lead as the default robot brain — Chinese robotics firm Galbot became the latest adopter this month, integrating Jetson AGX Thor into its G1 Premium humanoid alongside existing users spanning Agility, Boston Dynamics, Figure and Caterpillar. Physical Intelligence is reportedly in talks for a new ~$1B round at a valuation north of $11B — nearly double the $5.6B mark from its round just four months earlier — sharpening the software-layer race with Skild AI's "Skild Brain 1.0."

themes.title: China scaling & listing
themes.description: Unitree is now a live, trading public company after its record-oversubscribed Shanghai debut, joining BYD's incoming "Xiao Di" humanoid in a crowded field of 150+ Chinese startups. Agibot said it has now rolled out its 10,000th humanoid, doubling output, while LimX Dynamics' $200M Series B is funding scale-up of its COSA operating system ahead of a planned Hong Kong listing.

bear_case.title: Bubble warnings from serious sources
bear_case.description: China's NDRC has warned of a humanoid "bubble"; Morgan Stanley flags a wide gap between "dancing robots" and robots with scalable practical value. Global humanoid shipments reached roughly 19,000-22,000 units in H1 2026 (+272-300% YoY per Counterpoint) — real growth, but still a fraction of the volume implied by the sector's funding and valuation levels.

bear_case.title: Marks — public or private — don't always hold
bear_case.description: Unitree's own debut showed how fast a mark can move: shares opened +629% before paring to +460% by the close, an implied ~857x 2026 earnings versus the STAR Market's ~130x average. Figure's Forge secondary prices already imply a softer number than its $39B primary round. A real trade can correct a mark overnight, in either direction.

bear_case.title: Demos ≠ autonomy
bear_case.description: If a humanoid demo isn't explicitly labeled autonomous, assume teleoperation. Dexterity, inference speed, reliability, and cost still confine real use to structured factory/warehouse tasks.

bear_case.title: Crowding & shakeout risk
bear_case.description: 150+ companies chasing humanoids; a reshuffling of startups is widely expected. Robotics pioneer Rodney Brooks argues much of the investment will be wasted.

bear_case.title: A beat doesn't protect the stock
bear_case.description: Symbotic beat and raised in its Q3 FY26 print, then fell ~25% in a week anyway after a surprise dilutive share offering and a reaffirmed Barclays Sell rating. Intuitive Surgical dropped 5.8% on a cautious outlook despite an analyst upgrade days earlier. In parts of this sector, balance-sheet and guidance signals are doing more work than the headline earnings number.

bear_case.title: Revenue is elsewhere
bear_case.description: Industrial, logistics, and surgical robots generate proven revenue today; humanoids largely don't yet. Component and warehouse names carry less thesis risk than humanoid pure-plays.

bear_case.title: China price war
bear_case.description: Unitree's $5,900 R1 signals aggressive price compression that could squeeze Western OEM margins before the market matures — and 150+ Chinese humanoid startups, now including BYD, are competing on price and scale.

bear_case.title: "Dot-com stage" warnings
bear_case.description: KB Securities likened 2026's robotics/space enthusiasm to the final stage of the dot-com bubble; Ray Dalio separately compared the broader AI bubble to 1929 and 2000 valuation extremes. Sector EV/EBITDA multiples ranged from 0.9x (mature industrials) to 78.2x (speculative pure-plays) in Q4 2025 — a valuation split investors should not treat as one trade.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: Jetson Thor is now GA with 2M+ developers, and Chinese robot maker Galbot began integrating Jetson AGX Thor into its G1 Premium humanoid this month — the default compute layer keeps widening. Also your largest AI-sleeve holding and appears in your Quantum and Biotech sleeves too — don't triple-count the exposure.

positions.name: Rockwell Automation
positions.note: The cleanest listed US factory-automation exposure, benefiting from ~$200B in announced US factory buildouts, without a single-name dilution or guidance-shock risk like the ones that hit Symbotic and Fanuc this year.

positions.name: Teradyne
positions.note: Robotics segment just posted its first-ever $100M quarter (+33% YoY) and unveiled the MiR1200 Pallet Jack, its first physical-AI product, alongside a new Michigan cobot/AMR manufacturing hub — sustained, diversified execution rather than a single make-or-break bet.

positions.name: AeroVironment
positions.note: Fiscal Q4 revenue more than doubled to $641.6M and beat EPS by ~25%, and the new 100%/25% Trump-administration drone tariffs (effective Aug 14) give US makers a durable pricing edge. Also sits in your Defense sleeve — size across both, not in each.

positions.name: Kratos Defense
positions.note: New Army Javelin seeker-upgrade contract and a potential $156M DOE Solar Shield award add to a raised FY26 guide, with the same drone-tariff tailwind as AeroVironment. Also counts against your Defense sleeve.

positions.name: Tesla
positions.note: Musk now says Optimus output will be 'quite slow' given 10,000 unique new parts on an all-new line, with early units routed to an internal 'Optimus Academy' rather than customers — a full year into the conversion, production is still unverified.

positions.name: Harmonic Drive
positions.note: Lifted its full-year guidance Aug 7 on strong automation demand, then struck a more cautious note in its Aug 19 Q1 FY2027 report — still 7-buy/1-sell with an average ¥7,431 target, but the strain-wave-reducer bottleneck story needs the humanoid order book to keep converting.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: Q2 revenue grew 89% YoY to $108.5M and shares rose 16.4% over the week on a defense offtake deal and Canaccord roadmap commentary, but the company is still GAAP-loss-making as magnet-ramp costs bite. Also anchors your Critical Minerals sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Symbotic
positions.note: Shares fell roughly 25% this week after a surprise offering of 6.5M Class A shares plus 3.5M more from a SoftBank-controlled holder, and Barclays reaffirmed its Sell rating even after a beat-and-raise quarter — dilution and a fresh Sell call are enough to pause here despite real revenue growth.

positions.name: Cognex
positions.note: HSBC cut its rating to Hold from Buy and slashed its price target to $65 from $94 this week; the underlying machine-vision business still looks intact (a new dividend just went ex-date Aug 20), but the valuation call argues for waiting.

positions.name: Intuitive Surgical
positions.note: Shares fell 5.8% on Aug 20 on a cautious outlook despite an Oppenheimer upgrade, and J&J's Ottava has now cleared FDA review for a full slate of soft-tissue procedures — the competitive threat that was 'pressing the case' last week is now actually on the market. Down ~30% YTD and headed for its weakest year since 2008.

positions.name: Deere & Co
positions.note: The autonomy kit is real and revenue-generating, but robotics is a rounding error next to the ag cycle you would actually be buying.

positions.name: Caterpillar
positions.note: Five-machine autonomous lineup rolling out — same problem as Deere: construction demand dominates the return.

positions.name: Fanuc
positions.note: Shares are holding near ¥6,720 with a 9-buy/1-sell analyst split after the Aug 3 crash, but a bounce and a limit-up week for peers isn't a re-rating yet. Wait for the volatility to actually settle.

positions.name: Keyence
positions.note: Exceptional margins and permanently expensive; this week's limit-up rally just reinforces that the price already assumes a lot. Needs a genuine de-rating before the maths works.

positions.name: ABB Ltd
positions.note: Selling the robotics division to SoftBank for $5.375B — still awaiting regulatory clearance and not yet closed, which removes most of the reason it was on this list.

positions.name: Serve Robotics
positions.note: Shares fell another ~14% on Aug 18 on top of last month's guidance cut (to $9-10M from $26M) as the Uber relationship resets beyond early 2027 — stock is now down ~80% from its 2024 peak even as it pivots to DoorDash and Grubhub.

positions.name: Ouster
positions.note: Q2 revenue accelerated 56% YoY to $55M and a new Econolite/Utah DOT contract (160 intersections) show real, diversifying demand beyond automotive lidar — enough to keep this off Avoid, though commodity pricing pressure keeps it out of Core or Speculative.

positions.name: UiPath
positions.note: RPA is being disrupted by the same AI agents it claims to ride, and the robotics label is marketing rather than hardware.
